title: Characterization of Alternative Holobiont States in Ulcerative Colitis to Pave the Way for Innovative Treatment Strategies
official: Characterization of Alternative Holobiont States in Ulcerative Colitis to Pave the Way for Innovative Treatment Strategies (CHARTS)
summary: Ulcerative colitis (UC) results from a dynamic imbalance between the intestinal microbiota, the epithelial barrier and the immune system. In a pediatric UC cohort, the team identified alternative stable states (ASS) of the intestinal ecosystem: favourable, diverse states associated with remission, and depleted and dysbiotic states associated with active disease and a higher risk of treatment failure or relapse. CHARTS is a prospective, multicentric cohort that aims to translate and validate the concept of alternative holobiont states in adult UC patients who are naive to biotherapy and for whom a biotherapy is indicated as standard of care. One hundred patients will be followed for one year (visits at W0, W14, W30, W52) with longitudinal clinical data, blood and fecal samples and 2-3 standard-of-care endoscopies. Fecal microbiota will be characterized by sequencing and intestinal inflammation by fecal calprotectin. The project will build an integrative reference framework of intestinal ecosystem states and an algorithm to attribute a microbiota state from a single fecal sample, in order to identify patients likely to benefit from future microbiota-targeting (symbio-) therapy. No symbiotherapy will be initiated or proposed during the study.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* UC diagnostic confirmed from more than 6 months
* Patient aged of 18 years old minimum
* Patient naïve from any biotherapy for UC treatment
* Patient for whom a biotherapy treatment is scheduled in standard care. In the case of pregnancy, treatment will be managed in accordance with guidelines and standards of care. As anti-TNF agents and vedolizumab are authorised for use in all phases of pregnancy, this condition does not justify an exclusion criterion.
* Informed consent signed

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients with a CD or indetermined colitis disease
* Incapacity of study procedure understanding
* Patient has received antibiotics during the last 3 months before inclusion
* Patient has a known psychiatric disorder that would interfere with proper cooperation with the requirements of the study.
* Patient is a regular user of illicit or recreational drugs or has had a recent history (within the last year) of drug or alcohol abuse or dependence
* Patient is currently committed to an institution by virtue of an order issued either by the judicial or administrative authorities.
